http://www.control-escape.com/linux/lx-partition.html
It's a great distro for beginners who aren't after lightness.

It's probably the best distro for a beginner. Cinnamon (mint's default desktop) Is quite user friendly, and since Mint is Ubuntu based you get the benefits of *Buntu's repos and of the PPA system. Honestly you should try the various *buntu flavors besides Mint to see what you like best. Lubuntu and Xubuntu both make for lean mean *buntu machines, and Kubuntu has KDE, which some folks love. (Personally I use Mint)

Once you're comfy with *buntus, you might wanna try plain ol' Debian for something more universal, or try Bunsen Labs for something delightfully minimalist. (BL is the successor to #!, aka CrunchBang) Arch and Gentoo are distros to try once you get some experience under yer belt.

On the subject of Arch, while it is not babby's first Distro, it does have a VERY useful wiki with help for all sorts of issues here: https://wiki.archlinux.org/ If you have an issue with something, you'll likely find a solution or five on the Archwiki.

Other sources of aid include Mint's IRC channel, The Ubuntu forums, and the various linux related stack exchanges: http://askubuntu.com/ http://elementaryos.stackexchange.com/ http://raspberrypi.stackexchange.com/ http://superuser.com/ http://unix.stackexchange.com/
